title: With high probability the random subgraph has one component containing every non-isolated vertex, and its isolated vertices are far apart

core_obligations: Set up the two rounds: the proof fixes p_2 as the inverse square of the dimension parameter and chooses p_1 so that the two rounds multiply to the correct complement, then checks that the expected count of isolated vertices in the first round differs from the original one by a factor tending to one, using the expansion estimate (proof lines 542-549).

Apply the two established lemmas: the proofs of the separation statement and the gap statement hold in the extended regime of the range for p, so they apply to the first round, and Markov's inequality shows fewer than half the vertices are isolated, so a non-isolated component exists (proof lines 550-551).

Condition and merge: conditioning on the event that every component of the first round is either isolated or large and that the isolated vertices are pairwise far apart, the proof shows that after sprinkling with the second probability all large components merge into one (proof lines 553-604).
Conclusion: the merged component contains every non-isolated vertex, and the vertices receiving no sprinkled edge remain isolated and still far apart, which is the statement (proof lines 603-605).
proof_roadmap: 两轮曝光：取 p_2 = d^{-2}，p_1 使 (1-p_1)(1-p_2) = 1-p；用展开估计核对第一轮的孤立点期望与原值只差 1+o(1) 的因子。
由分离引理与间隙引理在扩展区间仍成立，可对第一轮套用；条件于「每个分量要么孤立要么阶 ≥ d^20，且孤立点两两距离 ≥ 3」，再证明第二轮的撒边把所有大分量并成一个；未获撒边的点保持孤立且仍两两远离。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the connectivity proposition of the random part (author proposition at source lines 536-539, label prop:unique-component): with high probability there is a unique component containing every non-isolated vertex, and the isolated vertices are pairwise at distance at least three. The proof (source lines 541-606) is the longest argument of that section and is a genuine two-round exposure: it splits the edge probability into two rounds (proof lines 542-549), reuses the separation and gap lemmas in the extended regime together with Markov's inequality to obtain a non-isolated component (proof lines 550-551), and then shows that the second round merges all large components while keeping the remaining isolated vertices far apart (proof lines 553-605). The merging step, carried out component by component, is the content. H2.
